questions.q: What is the fictional database and company at the center of this capstone?
options: Meridian Outfitters' MeridianRetail database
A fictional bank's core ledger database
An unnamed Azure SQL Database
The AdventureWorks sample database
questions.explain: Meridian Outfitters is an outdoor gear retailer whose order system lives in the MeridianRetail database — the scenario used across all six capstone lessons.

questions.q: Which stored procedure powers the MeridianConnect Order History panel that reps report timing out?
options: dbo.usp_CustomerOrderHistory
dbo.usp_GetOrderTotals
dbo.usp_WholesaleReport
dbo.usp_RefreshInventory
questions.explain: dbo.usp_CustomerOrderHistory selects a customer's trailing-12-month orders from dbo.Orders and is the procedure behind the slow screen.

questions.q: Why did dbo.Orders grow from roughly 2 million to roughly 14 million rows over three years?
options: Mostly because of a B2B wholesale program launched 18 months ago, where accounts place far more orders than typical consumers
Because Meridian migrated from a different database engine
Because of a data entry bug that duplicated rows
Row growth is unrelated to the performance problem
questions.explain: Wholesale accounts like TrailWorks Co-op place thousands of orders a year rather than a consumer's typical few dozen, which is central to why certain accounts trigger the slowdown.

questions.q: What specific pattern do reps report about when the Order History panel is slow?
options: Intermittent, worst between 10 AM and 2 PM, and concentrated on specific accounts
It is uniformly slow for every customer at all times of day
It only fails overnight during backup jobs
It fails only on the first login of the day
questions.explain: The symptom is load-correlated and account-specific — a real clue, not vague noise, that narrows where to look.

questions.q: Per this lesson, why shouldn't you act on a guess like "it's probably a missing index" right now?
options: Because Chapter 1's measure-identify-change-verify loop exists specifically to stop you from making changes before you've measured the real bottleneck
Because missing indexes never cause performance problems
Because guesses are always correct, so there is nothing to verify
Because MeridianConnect does not support index changes
questions.explain: This capstone exists to walk the full loop for real — the next lesson gathers a baseline and reads the actual plan and wait stats before any change is proposed.
